analyses.t: FX Outlook 2027: Seven key calls
analyses.x: We expect 2027 to be a low-volatility year in FX, with central banks and rate differentials firmly in the driving seat. We see a dollar decline resuming from 2Q27, while diverging monetary, growth and external dynamics create opportunities across regions

analyses.t: FX Outlook 2027: Seven key risks
analyses.x: EUROPE: Low volatility masks a wide range of tail risks for 2027. AI stress, another inflation shock, fiscal concerns, elections and geopolitical escalation could all trigger sharp FX moves, while financial repression and a carry unwind add further asymmetric risks

analyses.t: FX volatility in 2027: In need of shock therapy
analyses.x: EUROPE: Why is FX volatility so low? Even a 6% fall in the Nasdaq barely budges USD/JPY these days. Have FX markets found a general equilibrium, or is there some kind of separation between geopolitics and macro? We think the answer lies more in the structure of FX trading and do not rule out jump risk if the shock is big enough

analyses.t: G10 FX Outlook 2027: It’s hard to look beyond the Fed
analyses.x: EUROPE: In a very uncertain world, this year’s more hawkish steer from the Federal Reserve has provided a constant and supportive anchor for the dollar. While the immediate picture for the dollar looks quite constructive, a turn in the inflation cycle by the second half of 2027 should usher in a modest downtrend

analyses.t: EMEA FX Outlook 2027: Restrictive policy remains the key FX anchor
analyses.x: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: EMEA FX should remain supported by restrictive policy and attractive carry, but performance will increasingly diverge. We favour HUF, ZAR and TRY, while CZK remains supported and PLN faces headwinds. Global yields, energy prices, fiscal risks and geopolitics remain key drivers

analyses.t: Asia FX Outlook 2027: Rotation underway but tech currencies should lead
analyses.x: ASIA/PACIFIC: The recent sell-off in oil prices has provided some much-needed relief to South Asian currencies. Looking into 2027, and assuming the dollar does start to soften, we prefer to back the tech-linked currencies of North Asia. These currencies are backed by large current account surpluses – surpluses which could be coming home

analyses.t: Latam FX Outlook 2027: Banxico abandons the peso
analyses.x: LATIN AMERICA: It has been a mixed year for Latam FX, where only the higher yields of the Brazilian real and Mexican peso have allowed those currencies to deliver a net total positive return against the dollar. In 2027, we think the real can outperform the forwards, but are worried about Banxico’s neglect of the peso. Chile’s peso might prove a little more resilient, too
